sources.title: Palace Museum: Northern Liang
sources.note: Original museum text indexed and read; direct retrieval failed. Records 397 uprising, Duan Ye, Juqu succession and 412 Guzang. Ethnicity is not simplified into a settled modern identity.

sources.title: Tong Chunyan, National Museum of China: Buddhist voices in Liangzhou
sources.note: Direct full curator essay read. Uses 401 accession, Hexi refugee and scholarly context only. Same-museum related object entry conservatively combined with this essay for work-level budgeting.

sources.title: National Museum of China: Bai Shuangju stone stupa
sources.note: Direct object entry read, paragraphs 1-3: 434 inscription, components, tenon, images and texts, migration of craftsmen. Do not assign the trigrams on other examples to this object or infer its original ritual placement.

sources.title: Shu-fen Liu: New Perspectives on the Suppression of Buddhism during the Northern Wei (2001)
sources.note: Direct author abstract read, paragraphs 3-4: 439 conquest, forced resettlement and Juqu brothers at Gaochang. Omits deportee number because English abstract says supporters while another source says households.

sources.title: Gansu Provincial Museum exhibition report: Five Liang historical culture
sources.note: Direct museum-authored exhibition report read. Paragraphs on dated artifacts, cloth list, Gaochang continuation to 460, Sixteen Kingdoms Pan Yue manuscript and southward route. Earlier Wei/Jin tomb paintings not presented as specifically Northern Liang households.

sources.title: Pei Chengguo: The Silk Road and the Economy of Gaochang (2017)
sources.note: Direct scholarly article PDF read, printed pp.41 and48. Uses only explicitly Northern Liang-period silk and wheat records; later sixth/seventh-century household purchase, waste passage, inns, silver payments and cocoon payments excluded. Turfan location outside atlas polygon is public.

sources.title: Dunhuang Academy: Introduction to the Mogao Caves
sources.note: Direct institutional page read: opening geology and cave-type section1, Cave268 meditation cells. Later north-area living caves with stoves not generalized to Northern Liang.

sources.title: Guo, Staff and colleagues: A new approach to the chronology of caves 268, 272 and 275 (2018)
sources.note: Direct original Radiocarbon paper read, abstract, sample tables and conclusions. Bayesian modeled 410-440 CE is a study result, not an exact universal foundation date; plant fibers sampled from statue cores/rendering.

sources.title: Poh Yee Wong: Acculturation as Seen Through Buddha’s Birthday Parades in Northern Wei Luoyang (2012)
sources.note: Direct University of the West dissertation read, printed p.223, PDF index234/page235, footnotes1037-1038. Chinese short excerpt and parallel English account from Jiuquan429 stupa; modern scholarly typesetting, not a photographed rubbing. Avoid potentially erroneous 報思 and uncertain name-character transcription outside chosen phrase.

proposedOverrides.name: Northern Liang
proposedOverrides.summary: A Hexi Corridor kingdom whose political reach and Buddhist workshops linked northwestern China with Central Asia.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact single indexed ID only; no aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.historicalSpan: 397-439 in Gansu; Juqu continuation farther west to460.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-400 Polygon, bbox94.64674646746471,37.22811540715641,103.8016380163802,41.50825703486663. Hexi/Gansu outline does not cover Gaochang/Turfan. Public overview and regional household passages distinguish that geography.
batchIdentityNotes.boundaries: Distinct from Southern Liang and later southern Liang dynasty. north-liang and juqu not indexed. No successor links because appropriate event geometry has not been checked.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: identity.json stores exact index, decoded feature properties, runtime absence and staged checks. Chronology supported by Palace Museum, NMC, Liu and Gansu Museum. No household medicine or toilet practices inferred from later Gaochang documents.
